content: Dig the well before you are parched with thirst.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Lin ke jue jing (临渴掘井) — Huangdi Neijing & Zhu Zi Jia Xun
explanation: To begin digging into bedrock when your throat is already dry and delirious with dehydration is the height of folly. True wisdom builds health before sickness arrives, establishes financial resilience before famine strikes, and deepens spiritual roots before the storm hits.
practicalInsight: Identify one vulnerability in your current routine—financial, physical, or relational—and take one preventative safeguard today.
reflectionPrompt: What 'well' have you neglected to dig, assuming the rains of good fortune will never dry up?
